statement: If an affine hyperbolic curve of proper genus at least2 has potential good curve reduction at coefficient p with special p-rank at least2, every arithmetically normalized procyclic pro-p subgroup is cuspidal. For any degree-d cover of the original punctured Gaussian elliptic curve this holds whenever p=1 mod4 and the proper curve has potential good reduction, in particular for every p>d with p=1 mod4.
depends_on: A.55 local Prym and integral transfer arguments
answers: Task A.5: a general good-curve-reduction normalizer criterion
Task A.5: every degree-d cover at all coefficient primes p>d with p=1 mod4
notes: Root and DE independently read the full proof, reopened the primary Tate and SGA1 passages, and reran the exact certificate: PASS. Registered after both audits.  The generic Tate specialization kernel is saturated; no CM or arithmetic connected–étale splitting is assumed. A mod-p union-of-two-proper-subspaces argument selects actual Picard torsion retaining exact special order, and cyclic p^n cover Pryms have interior slopes by Raynaud. The f=1 case for covers of ordinary E uses the actual punctured map and a p-rank-zero Prym. Potential good CURVE reduction, not merely good Jacobian reduction, is required. Galois closure subgroup S_d and prime-to-p specialization prove the uniform degree bound. No full fixed-subgroup or universal all-prime assertion.
